_readme: Durable annotation layer for scraped/mirrored documents. scrapers/build_index.py merges these in AFTER every loader, so they survive any re-scrape or rebuild. Each override targets exactly one doc via match (all listed fields must equal the doc's — convention is src+f for library/PDF docs, src+p for scraped web docs with no filename); s_append is added to the card summary, extra_chunks are added to the search index. Nothing else is touched. Added 19 Sep 2026 for the Data Migration Tool <-> UDF Configuration cross-links (see ROADMAP.md Technical Debt). Extended 7 Oct 2026 for the "Support made simple in PeopleXD" / Access Digital Assistant / MyAccess Portal article (first override matched on src+p rather than src+f).

overrides.s_append: See also: if the Data Migration Tool reports this UDF upload as Complete / 0 Failed but a colleague can't see the uploaded values on the employee record, that is not a Data Migration Tool problem — check the UDF Configuration guide's Employee Search Person Filter (Active/Dormant) and the Data Labels "Active" checkbox on the UDF field itself. See Kevin's Guides: "HOW TO: Troubleshoot — UDF Data Uploaded Successfully but Not Visible on Employee Records".
extra_chunks: Troubleshooting cross-reference (added by Kevin's HR Systems team, 19 Sep 2026): if this Data Migration Tool upload for User Defined Fields shows Complete / 0 Failed but a colleague reports they can't see the uploaded values on the employee's live record, do not assume the upload failed silently or the data is wrong. Check, in order: (1) the Employee Search "Person Filter" on the People Management Dashboard — defaults to Active only, so a dormant/leaver record won't appear regardless of the data; (2) the UDF's own Data Labels "Active" checkbox in HR Admin Setup Settings > User Defined Objects > [Reference Code] > Data Labels — if unchecked, the field won't display for anyone even though the value uploaded successfully. See Kevin's Guides: "HOW TO: Troubleshoot — UDF Data Uploaded Successfully but Not Visible on Employee Records" for the full order and what to rule out (Security Required, CorePortal Display, and the migration job's own Public/Private flag are not the cause).

overrides.s_append: The Access Digital Assistant (ADA) is Access Group's automated support chatbot for PeopleXD. It gives instant answers, troubleshooting steps and relevant help content 24/7, and escalates to a human support agent when it can't resolve something — out-of-hours queries are still logged and answered when the team is back. ADA is only available to named support contacts for your organisation. There are two ways to reach it: (1) Via PeopleXD — click the Access Digital Assistant icon, select "Ask a question", type the query, then review the guidance given or the suggested help articles. (2) Via the MyAccess Portal — sign in to MyAccess, click the Access Digital Assistant icon, select the relevant product/module, ask the question, then review the results. This MyAccess Portal route is the one shown step-by-step in the article's own embedded walkthrough video, "MyAccess Portal ADA.mp4". Best practice when asking ADA a question: keep it short and clear, ask from within the relevant product/module for tailored guidance, and never include a specific individual's personal data in the question (e.g. ask the general "How do I check user login history?" rather than naming a particular person). Raised cases appear under Tickets, where you can track progress, reply, or download a transcript. ADA asks for feedback at the end of a conversation to help route things correctly. What support you can access depends on your organisation's Customer Success Plan (CSP) tier; named contacts on any CSP can use ADA, and anyone else should ask their own organisation's named contact to raise it on their behalf.
extra_chunks: Access Digital Assistant (ADA) in PeopleXD — what it is: Access Group's automated support assistant for PeopleXD, giving instant answers to common questions, troubleshooting steps, and relevant help content, available 24/7. Only available to named support contacts for your organisation. If ADA can't resolve an issue it escalates to Access's human support team; queries raised outside normal hours are still passed to the team and answered when they return. Source: Intercom article "Support made simple in PeopleXD" (13916885).

How to use the Access Digital Assistant via PeopleXD itself: click the Access Digital Assistant icon within PeopleXD, select "Ask a question", type your question, then review the guidance given or the suggested help articles it returns.

How to use the Access Digital Assistant via the MyAccess Portal — this is the exact walkthrough shown in the article's "MyAccess Portal ADA.mp4" video: sign in to the MyAccess Portal, click the Access Digital Assistant icon, select the relevant product or module, type your question, then review the results it returns.

Best practice for asking the Access Digital Assistant a question in PeopleXD or MyAccess Portal: keep the question short and clear, and ask it from within the specific product/module you need help with so the guidance is tailored to that area. Do not include a specific individual's personal data in a question — e.g. ask the general "How do I check user login history?" rather than naming a specific person, since the assistant is not the right channel for case-specific personal data.

Viewing and managing PeopleXD support tickets raised via the Access Digital Assistant or support: open the Tickets section to check progress on an open case, reply to it, or download a transcript of the conversation.

What PeopleXD/Access support you can access depends on your organisation's Customer Success Plan (CSP) — the level of support your organisation has contracted with Access Group, which determines what support is available and how many people can raise cases. Named support contacts on any CSP tier can use the Access Digital Assistant; if you are not a named contact, ask your organisation's named contact to raise the query for you. Not all Access products currently support CSPs, but it is being rolled out to all.
